scenes.headline: How a video model learns to move a robot arm
scenes.sub: Praxis-1 reads motion off a future it is still imagining
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Wystan! Praxis-1 is Runway's open robot policy. Here's how a video model ends up driving an arm.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: A big video model imagines the next 1.6 seconds, and a small action expert reads its layers to produce the motion for those seconds.
scenes.say: The idea: a big video model imagines the next moment, and a small action expert reads its layers to work out the motion.

steps.say: Each call takes an instruction, the latest frames from two cameras, and where the arm is right now.
A mixture of experts video model starts denoising the next stretch of video, chunk by chunk.

steps.note: nothing flows back into the video model
steps.say: A small action expert taps eight of its layers, reading the future as the backbone imagines it.
Out come twenty-four rows of motion: one point six seconds at fifteen hertz.

items.say: Sampling starts from pure noise, for both the video and the actions.
The first Euler step only moves the video a little. It is still mostly noise.
The second step jumps straight to clean actions. By default the video is never finished.
The arm executes the chunk, and the frames it saw become the next call's context.

scenes.title: Learn the world, then the arm

items.say: Training starts with a general video model.
Then video of hands and robots, where each chunk only sees the past.
Then the action expert joins, and video stays in the loss.
Finally a full fine-tune for each robot.

scenes.title: RoboLab-120 task success
scenes.note: fifth overall; first among world action models
scenes.say: On a hundred and twenty simulated tasks it scores forty-six point two percent. That's first among world action models, and fifth on the full board.

scenes.text: The robot moves on a future the model has barely started imagining, so better imagination is where the errors live.
scenes.say: The robot moves on a future the model has barely started imagining. That imagination is where the remaining errors live.

recap: Video backbone imagines, action expert reads
Two Euler steps, 1.6 s per chunk
scenes.say: A video model that imagines, an expert that reads it, two steps per chunk.
